title: RecyclerView 内存优化：ViewHolder、Prefetch、Pool 与图片峰值
key_conclusions: RecyclerView memory optimization starts by separating idle, slow scroll, fling, image entry, and post-scroll recovery windows.
RecycledViewPool size must be tied to viewport needs and measured creation cost, not increased blindly.
Image decode size, bitmap reuse, cache caps, and request cancellation usually dominate list memory peaks.
A valid memory fix must preserve scroll frame time and avoid moving the peak into first interaction.
shallow_points: The article does not include a real scripted scroll trace.
It does not validate GapWorker or RecyclerView internals against a specific AndroidX version.
It does not quantify pool cap tradeoffs for multiple device RAM classes.
It does not include real image-loader cache statistics from Glide or Coil.
discovered_connections: Day 69's T0-T5 startup model maps directly to list idle, slow scroll, fling, image entry, and recovery windows.
Day 68's cross-validation remains necessary when image memory appears across Java heap, Native heap, Graphics, and dma-buf.
Day 66's shared owner proof applies to graphics buffers created while scrolling.
Day 71 should reuse Day 67 memcg and Day 68 attribution when splitting RecyclerView cost across app processes.
suggest_future_topics: Day 71 should focus on multi-process memory benefits, accounting costs, and lmkd risk.
A future lab should provide a repeatable RecyclerView fling script with Perfetto markers.
A future article should compare Glide, Coil, and Fresco cache and bitmap pool evidence.
A future checklist should include pool caps by viewport, density, image size, and item type.
knowledge_gaps: Need real Perfetto and allocation traces for RecyclerView fling cases.
Need AndroidX version-specific validation for GapWorker and pool behavior.
Need measured bitmap/cache tradeoffs on low-RAM devices.
Need source-backed comparison across common image loading libraries.
